messages:
maria: CI failures on infra repo — terraform apply in GH Actions keeps failing on our self-hosted runners with 'no space left on device'. This is blocking the gpu-nodepool scale-up canary.

jon: ugh, can you paste the runner logs?

maria: here's the tail of the GH Action job log:
```
Run terraform init
# ...
Error: failed to fetch provider: write /tmp/terraform-plugin-plugin: no space left on device
/bin/checkout failed: exit code 1
```

maria: and df -h on the runner after the job died:
```
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/nvme0n1p1  50G   49G   200M  100% /
tmpfs           7.8G     0  7.8G   0% /run/user/1000
```

devops-bot: Runner metadata: labels: [self-hosted,gpu,small-disk], runner version: 2.299.1, recent jobs: large-artifact-upload

jon: looks like the runner image is too small and artifacts from model-checks are filling disk. Were we caching model artifacts into the repo? :thinking:

alex: we saw a big tar in repo_artifacts/model_evals.tar (~12GB) from last perf test. GH Actions does a full checkout by default; combine that with terraform provider downloads and plugin cache = boom.

sre-kate: this explains why nodepool scale-up can't finish: terraform apply fails, state lock remains for ~10m, then next apply times out and cancels the canary. We need quick mitigation to unstick the rollout.

maria: short-term: disable concurrent runs on infra repo with `concurrency: group: infra-${{ github.ref }}` and add `if: github.actor != 'model-bot'` to skip model pushes. Also add a pre-step to prune large files: `git lfs prune` and run `du -sh . | sort -h | tail -n 10`.

jon: longer-term: 1) increase runner root disk to 200GB for gpu-labeled runners, 2) change actions/checkout to `fetch-depth: 1` or use partial clone for large LFS objects, 3) move model artifacts to S3 and reference them in CI, 4) add a disk-usage check in runner health monitor.

alex: also add terraform remote state lock timeout increase and better retry backoff in GH job to avoid canary stalls. Maybe switch nodepool scaling to plan + manual apply for now.

sre-kate: I'll open a quick PR to set concurrency and fetch-depth, and I'll patch the auto-deploy workflow to require manual approval when `module.gpu_nodepool.min_size` increases. Ping me if someone wants to pair on the runner resize.

maria: thanks. temp workaround applied. canary resumed after the manual retry. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Note: job 12345 auto-cancelled due to concurrency rule change.

jon: follow-up ticket to infra backlog: runner disk resize + move model artifacts off-repo + terraform backoff tuning. Assigning to eng-infra ops.

maria: adding a short blameless note in #incidents.
